# SPE Round 3 Plan

Round 2 hit 1 prediction out of 5. The naive "same as last round" guess beat my predictions 4 times out of 5. The stability streak is 0, so round 3 cannot end the loop. Round 3 makes one change to config C, adds a separate slice of hard tickets, runs 5 trials per cell instead of 3, and drops config D. My round 3 predictions stay close to the round 2 numbers unless a specific failure gives a reason to expect a shift.

## Inputs read before planning

- `spe/prediction-log.md`, round 2 section. Only A's category accuracy was a hit. The Why that broke was C's "merged tools cut wrong tool choice."
- `spe/failures.md`. F4 (outage lookup hidden) is open. F5 (grader read priority from the draft reply) is fixed, and round 2 was regraded. F6 (Haiku retries doubled tokens) is open.
- The "Proposed for round 3" table in `spec.md` (P1 to P4).
- `spe/predictions/r03-draft.yaml`. Its round 2 category baselines are A 0.86, B 0.86, C 0.80, and D 0.74.

## Problems I found in the round 2 evidence

1. **The r01 priority baseline may use the old grader.** F5 appeared in round 2. If round 1 also read priority from the draft reply, then the 0.78 in the "same as last round" column is not comparable with C's regraded 0.71. The harness steps below regrade round 1 if its transcripts exist.
2. **P2 changes the task set for every config.** If I mix the 10 hard tickets into the core set, the round 2 baselines stop applying. I will score the hard tickets as a separate slice. The core set stays the same as round 2.
3. **F4 explains C's priority misses. It does not clearly explain C's category drop.** The category prediction for C therefore assumes only partial recovery.
4. **Round 2 predictions had no stated error.** The stop rule needs predictions to match results "within their stated error." Every round 3 prediction has an error band.

## 1. Specify

The specify step saves the user's prompt word for word in `spe/spec/transcripts/2026-10-21-r03.md`. The user gave no planning answers because the round runs autonomously. I will add any plan review corrections the user makes. That file is never edited after that.

## 2. Predict

These predictions use the core set (the round 2 tickets) unless a row says otherwise. The "Same as last round" column holds the r02 regraded numbers. "Hit" means the measured number falls within the stated error of the prediction.

Three cells use a change from round 2 (Δ) instead of an absolute number. This plan does not have A's and B's r02 priority or cost numbers. A and B are unchanged controls, so the prediction for each is "no change." The predict step reads the absolute r02 values from `spe/evals/results/r02/` and writes them into `r03.yaml` before the commit. It does not change the deltas.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Category accuracy, core | 0.86 | 0.86 | 0.82 | 0.86 / 0.86 / 0.80 | ±0.03 | `category_match` on the core set | A and B did not change. C gets the status result back as evidence for the outage category, but its other tools stay merged. So C closes part of the 0.06 gap to A and B, not all of it. |
| Priority accuracy, core | Δ 0.00 | Δ 0.00 | 0.78 | r02 A / r02 B / 0.71 | ±0.04 | `priority_match` on `label.priority` | F4 put C's outage tickets at P3. Calling the status check restores P1 and P2 on those tickets. |
| Status check call rate on outage tickets | 0.95 | 0.95 | 0.95 | not graded in r02 / not graded in r02 / 0.00 | ±0.05 | `status_called_on_outage` | C now has a separate tool with a clear name. A and B always had the tool separate. |
| Category accuracy, hard slice (10 tickets) | 0.70 | 0.70 | 0.66 | none (new slice) | ±0.10 | `category_match` on the hard set | Mixed tickets need a billing lookup, a status lookup, and the tie-break rule. C's remaining merged tool adds one more way to skip the billing lookup. |
| Cost per ticket, core | Δ 0% | Δ 0% | +10% vs r02 C | r02 A / r02 B / r02 C | ±15% | Harness token log × the price table in the harness | C makes one extra tool call on outage tickets. Nothing changed for A or B. |

How this round can fail:

- If C's priority stays inside 0.71 ± 0.04, P1 did not fix F4. The learn step then reopens the cause of F4.
- If A or B moves more than 0.05 from r02 on the core set, the environment drifted. Possible causes are a model version change or a harness change. The learn step must explain the drift before it trusts any C comparison.
- If any config scores above 0.90 on the hard slice, R29 fails, and the hard slice did not do its job.
- The calibration target is that my predictions tie or beat the naive column on at least 5 of the 9 core cells. Round 2 managed 1 of 5.

The predict step saves this plan as `spe/plans/r03.md`. It writes `spe/predictions/r03.yaml` with `status: committed`, the table above, the error bands, and the grader check name for each number. It marks `r03-draft.yaml` as `status: superseded` and drops its D 0.74 baseline. All of this happens before any harness work or trial.

### Workflow arguments

```js
  round: "r03",
  configs: ["A", "B", "C"],          // D dropped (P3, r03-Q1 default)
  ticketSets: {
    core: "spe/evals/tickets/core",  // same set as r02

  },

  models: "unchanged from r02 per config",
  helperAgentModel: "opus",          // labelers and any non-trial agents
  concurrency: 10,
  budgetCapUSD: 30,
  outDir: "spe/evals/results/r03/",
  grader: "spe/evals/harness/grade.py",
  haltOn: ["budget_cap", "answer_key_leak", "grader_error"]

```

### Cost and time estimate (unmeasured)

This estimate assumes about 30 core tickets. The real count comes from the r02 manifest. 40 tickets × 3 configs × 5 trials makes about 600 trial runs. At a guessed $0.01 per run, trials cost about $6. Labeling and grading add about $2. The total is about $8, under a cap of $30. At 10 runs at a time and about 30 seconds per run, the run takes about 30 minutes. None of these numbers have been measured.

### Halt conditions

- The budget cap of $30 is hit.
- A label or answer key turns up in any trial's context.
- The grader errors or returns a missing field on any graded file during the run.

On any of these, the harness stops the round and I report what happened. I will not patch the problem and continue.
